body:
Two more specimens, both on Linux with `claude-opus-5-5`, both right after launching a background subagent with the Agent tool. They add three things to the report above: the fabricated results did not match the real ones; one invented claim outlived its session in a memory file; and in one case Claude Code itself withdrew the fabricated response, because the tool call it claimed did not parse.

**1. Kept in the session JSONL (2.1.322, 2026-11-11, session `86bab0cb-f84a-4bcd-bb37-67d1c2cca300`).**

- 67 s after the Agent launch returned, assistant message `msg_011CgweSNAXtZx4E9XFRxnTJ` (18:54:01 UTC) contained a 16,900-character text block opening `<system-reminder>\n<task-notification>\n<task-id>…`, with the real task id and a full invented `<result>` report.
- The same message also carried a valid Bash `tool_use`, so the response was well-formed and was kept.
- The real notification for that agent arrived 18 minutes later (19:12:24), as a user record, with a different report.
- The invented report's specifics were largely wrong: version numbers, a config default, file and line references.
- What came of it: the session's own tool results, straight afterwards, contradicted those specifics, and the model worked from the tool results without ever remarking on the block. One claim survived, though. It appears only in the invented report and nothing in the session measured it, yet it was later written into a Claude Code auto-memory file as fact and repeated in the session's final report to me. I have since corrected the file.
- Form: the real notifications in both sessions carry `<tool-use-id>`, `<output-file>` and `<summary>`; this block has none of them, has no `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION` preamble, repeats a `<total_tokens>` element about a hundred times inside `<usage>`, and closes with a mismatched `</task-system-reminder>`.

**2. Withdrawn by Claude Code (2.1.325, 2026-11-14, session `bb495143-e813-4f4e-81d4-553c4c5f73f3`).**

- The first request after the Agent launch (sent 21:05:14 UTC, answered 21:05:46) returned text shaped as a `<task-notification>`: the real task id, an invented `tool-use-id`, `<status>completed</status>` and an invented report. It had `stop_reason: tool_use` and no parseable tool call.
- Claude Code treated that response as malformed. The session JSONL has no record of it, only the retry row at 21:05:46.387 ("The previous response failed to produce a valid tool call. Please retry the tool call now.") carrying its uuid in `retractedMessageUuids`. The retried response was normal.
- How I know what it contained: a plugin I run that redraws the transcript view kept the withdrawn response on screen, and I read it there; I have a screenshot of it. The stock view removes it.
- The real notification came at 21:32, 26 minutes after the fabricated one, with a different report. The invented report described a function that does not exist in the project.

What the pair shows for the detection suggestion at the end of the report:

- The second fabrication was removed only because the response claimed a tool call (`stop_reason: tool_use`) that did not parse. A fabrication in a response that carries a valid tool call, as the first did, or that simply ends the turn, as items 3 and 4 of the report did, is kept.
- Of the two patterns suggested, only `<task-notification>` matches the first block; it has no `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION` text.
- In both sessions the real notifications are user records, never assistant text, and both tasks were still running when the fabricated one appeared. So a check could go by who wrote the text and whether the task has finished, rather than by text patterns.

A related form on 2.1.327 with `claude-fable-5-2`, in case the request ids help: the model's whole reply is a copy of the wrapper Claude Code puts around a task notification, with no invented result.

Session `f5ed583a-95e5-426c-9b15-cb7927d763dc`, main thread, 2026-11-18 UTC. Five replies, each a single text block with no thinking, `stop_reason: end_turn`:

| time | request id | output tokens | text |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22:17:19 | `req_011ChBAgbQSKPxcGkAAQ7GeG` | 64 | `<system-reminder>`, `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]`, `This is an automated background-task event, NOT a message from the user.`, `</system-reminder>` |
| 22:27:29 | `req_011ChBBTa2bhisGQ7dnFyzpd` | 44 | `<system-reminder>`, `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]`, `</system-reminder>` |
| 22:38:04 | `req_011ChBCGVqtFfG99G6LVUUwf` | 44 | same |
| 22:49:54 | `req_011ChBDAmUBoco6pRDFcJCnE` | 44 | same |
| 23:05:39 | `req_011ChBENVXhLFFVVyPAzezEv` | 44 | same |

What the requests looked like:

- Each reply came at the end of a turn, several tool rounds in, while a background subagent of the session was still running. The message just before it was a tool result: an Agent launch result three times, a Bash result once, a SendMessage result once.
- For the first copy, the turn before had ended with no assistant text. So in the request that opened its turn, the last tool result and the incoming task notification sat in one user message, with no assistant turn between them: the tool result ran straight into the wrapper.
- From the second copy on, that was not the case. The previous copy was itself in the conversation as an assistant turn, and the notification was its own user message.
- Context at those requests was 760K to 825K tokens. I have not separated context size from this conversation's content as the trigger.

On the detection suggestion: 2.1.327 already scans main-thread assistant text for this kind of content and sends a telemetry event, `tengu_assistant_output_harness_content`. As far as I can read the code path, that is all it does: the text is not stripped or flagged, and nothing is retried.

One earlier specimen matches neither pattern the report suggests, since it has no `<task-notification>` and no `[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION`. On 2.1.302 with `claude-opus-5-5`, session `c891dafc-97d6-42ca-bd0f-374ae2743bf8`, `req_011Cg9tSmZedGafRtJxz4i4n`, 2026-10-18 14:49:18 UTC, three seconds after an Agent launch returned, the text block read `<system-reminder>The agent's result has been delivered as a task notification. Assistant turns written while it was running: none.</system-reminder>`. The same message carried a tool call to read queued notifications, which found none.
